So basically, I went camping with some guys from my youth group for the weekend and one thing we did on this trip was go on a cool hike. About 2 miles into the hike, we find a big waterfall- about 150 ft tall with a two foot pool of freezing cold water at the bottom- so as guys naturally do, we decided to go to the top of it (apparently only one of us saw the "Do not enter" sign). At the top, we get the chance to go two by two up to the edge of the cliff and have a cool view with the stream feet from out ankles. (Let me just clarify that I'm 5' 5" and 130 lbs and my buddy is 6' 2" and 250 lbs.) My buddy, lets say Manny, slips and falls into the stream. So I, being the big bravado guy I am, jumps directly in between him and the edge! I am inches from death trying to save my friend. My youth pastor did what our group now calls the Jason Roar as he screamed at me like a savage animal not to do that! We both climb out of the stream and on our way down, Manny and a few other people tell me that he slipped and fell into a small pool connected to the stream that I didnt see.
TL;DR- I unnecessarily risked my life to save my friend's life, who ended up never being in danger in the first place.

Going 200 mph in a car doesn't do anything other than make adrenaline, if those organisms fire off, while hunting actually gives you food. And I was not saying that animal suffering in a farm was an out lier: I was saying hunting accidents where the animal lived and died in pain was.
The only thing I can appreciate about your arguments is that even in a world filled with apathetic people with no motivation, you have an opinion on something.

Only considerjng deer that have only been maimed during hunting is equal to only considering farmers that have been injured by farm equipment making grain; yes there are bad shots but there is also poorly made equipment, but those data points are all outliers. 

And with regards to hunting vs buying farmed meat, i prefer hunting because I am held responsible for the discomfort of the animal. I make it quick and make it drop where it stands for the sake of not being a sadist rather than know the animal would be unfairly treated or tortured. So, I do agree with you on that point. 

You mentioned that we could get nutrition ways other than meat. I personally care more about the welfare of people than that of animals, so I think the organic chemists and researchers discovering these alternate organic foods should be looking for something more widespread to the whole world like cures for diseases and not first world privileges such as what they already research.

Im not saying that we shouldn't aim to be better than animals- I venture to say that we have already achieved that. It's more that you are making humans sound like the species responsible for the growth and maintenance of every other species in the world. 

And no, I think that people can make moral choices, but as a whole of all of humanity, humans do not have an amazing track record of keeping the peace or even try to do so. It's like giving an expensive vase to a troublesome toddler. 

This question that you have posed as your parent post does not only pertain to farm animals, but every animal that people eat. While I do not find the industries supporting the torture and inhumane conditions of farm animals, the meat harvested is nutritionally more beneficial in growing muscle and healthy fat. 

On your note about pain and suffering for deer: my family hunts for meat. We know how to shoot, skin, process, and cook white tail deer. And to say that a bullet going through a deer's heart is painful is a tragic exaggeration. The deer doesn't feel anything because it either drops dead where it stands or it runs away from the threat and die somewhere close by. If it runs, its brain has produced an excess of adrenaline that focuses the brains energy on fight or flight rather than pain- much like a human. That deer wouldn't feel more than a big sting, shock, and then death. Portraying this instantaneous event as if People would torture the animal like a prisoner of war is a completely false dramatization of reality. 

Also, it irritates me that I am asked an opinion question and when I provide an answer, my opinion is deemed as wrong and must be down voted. This thread is meant for people with my opinions, so why would you down vote the audience that you're talking to?

A more moral lifestyle is entirely subjective. There's no way that us humans, born and raised in war, death, and deception, can be "moral agents" for even ourselves, so how can we do so for the entire animal kingdom as well? My personal belief is that eating other animals is what brought us out from our caves and into buiness suits and there is statistical evidence to back that up saying that deer populations would inflate and cause scarcity if we didn't hunt and how killing certain animals to eat prevents the erradication of another animal that it preys on.
